Last updated: September 2026 · Prices and availability checked against Costco.com using an Austin, Texas ZIP code (78701) as a non-member (public pricing).

Disclosure: InHouse Wellness sells some of the same brands and comparable models discussed in this guide. Our recommendations are based on current product information, installation requirements, pricing, documented owner experiences, and the concrete service differences between retailers. Costco inventory, pricing, and availability can change, so confirm the live listing before you order.

A Costco sauna is usually a model line other retailers also sell, for less money, and whether it is worth it comes down to what Costco does not do. The hardware is usually solid. What catches buyers off guard is everything around the sticker price—the dedicated circuit, the 700-pound crate left at the curb, the assembly hours, and where support goes after Costco’s return window closes.

This review skips the generic “Costco-style sauna” language you’ll find elsewhere and names the exact models Costco is currently listing, their item numbers, current prices, electrical requirements, delivery terms, and warranty pathways. We also map each Costco unit to its InHouse Wellness equivalent so you can weigh a lower price against installation and specialist support. The core message: the word “Costco” matters far less than the specific SKU and what it costs you installed.

Quick verdict

  • Best current Costco sauna for most buyers: Dynamic Bellagio 3-person infrared — a 120V unit that fits most indoor spaces and installs without 240V wiring.
  • Best infrared model: Dynamic Bellagio 3-person (capacity and price) or San Marino Elite 2-person (if ultra-low-EMF marketing matters to you).
  • Best traditional/barrel model: Almost Heaven Morgan 4-person — red cedar with a Harvia heater and true 140–190°F heat.
  • Simplest installation: Dynamic Gracia 1–2 person — the lightest, most plug-and-play option.
  • Biggest hidden cost: electrical work. A 120V dedicated circuit is modest; a 240V barrel install can run four figures.
  • Main delivery warning: every current listing ships curbside freight only. The crate stops at your driveway.
  • Buy from Costco when: your electrical is already compatible, you can handle delivery and assembly, and you value the return policy.
  • Consider a specialist when: you want model-matching help, white-glove placement, installation coordination, or hands-on warranty support.

What Costco sells right now — and what it costs

Current Costco sauna model reviews

Rather than repeat the same electrical, delivery, and EMF notes under each model, this section focuses on what makes each unit different. Shared specifics (wiring, freight, warranty pathways) are covered once in their own sections below.

Dynamic Bellagio 3-Person Infrared

Item 100370044 · ~$1,999.99 with promo · Indoor infrared · Rated up to 3

  • Heater: nine low-EMF FAR carbon panels; Canadian hemlock cabin.
  • Electrical: 120V, 20A dedicated circuit (NEMA 5-20P). No 240V work needed.
  • EMF claim: manufacturer states under 10 mG at 6 inches from panels.
  • Max temperature: roughly 140°F (radiant infrared, not high ambient air).
  • Warranty: 5-year limited (see the warranty section for the wood/electronics distinction).

Best for: the buyer who wants a genuine 2–3 person indoor cabin without stepping up to 240V wiring.

Why it stands out: it hits the sweet spot of capacity, price, and 120V simplicity, which is why it’s our default pick for most buyers.

Main limitation: hemlock and basic controls are mid-tier, not luxury; infrared heat feels different from a traditional sauna (see temperature section).

Hidden-cost risk: if you don’t already have a dedicated 20A outlet where the sauna will sit, budget for an electrician.

Owner feedback: several owners describe reliable heat once wired correctly and reasonable long-term durability; the recurring complaints are curbside-delivery surprise and assembly taking longer than the marketing estimate.

Verdict: the strongest all-around infrared option for indoor use. The same model line is sold at InHouse Wellness, where it comes with model-to-space matching, lifetime customer support, and the option to bundle accessories or a red-light upgrade. Shop the Dynamic Bellagio 3-person infrared sauna, or step up to the higher-end Golden Designs Visby 3-person for near-luxury build quality at a fraction of a custom-sauna price.

Dynamic Gracia 1–2 Person Infrared

Item 100675807 · ~$1,799–$1,899 · Indoor infrared · Rated 1–2

  • Heater: low-EMF carbon panels; hemlock cabin; compact footprint.
  • Electrical: 120V plug-and-play into a dedicated circuit—the least demanding install in the lineup.
  • Max temperature: similar infrared range to the Bellagio (about 140°F max).

Best for: apartments, small rooms, and first-time infrared users who want the simplest possible setup.

Why it stands out: lighter panels make it the easiest unit to move from curb to room and to assemble solo or with one helper.

Main limitation: one to two people only, and fewer premium touches.

Hidden-cost risk: lowest of the group—often works on an existing dedicated 15–20A outlet if one is available and non-GFCI.

Owner feedback: owners consistently call out the easy footprint and quick assembly; expectations on capacity should stay realistic.

Verdict: the best value and simplest install. Shop the Dynamic Gracia 1–2 person infrared sauna at InHouse Wellness, or compare the Maxxus Seattle 2-person, which delivers better value than anything in Costco’s compact range.

Dynamic San Marino Elite 2-Person Infrared

Item 4000384560 · ~$2,299–$2,499 · Indoor infrared · Rated 2

  • Heater: carbon panels marketed as “ultra low EMF.”
  • Electrical: 120V dedicated circuit.

Best for: couples, and buyers for whom the lowest possible published EMF figure is a priority.

Why it stands out: the “ultra low EMF” positioning and two-person comfort sit a notch above the entry models.

Main limitation: you pay more for a two-person unit than the three-person Bellagio’s promo price; the EMF advantage is comparative marketing, not a proven health benefit (see EMF section).

Verdict: a reasonable pick if EMF marketing drives your decision, but weigh it against the Bellagio’s capacity. Shop the Dynamic San Marino Elite at InHouse Wellness, or—if you want true full-spectrum (near, mid, and far) infrared, which Costco doesn’t stock—the Maxxus S-Line 2-person full-spectrum sauna.

Almost Heaven Morgan 4-Person Barrel

Item 1324771 · ~$3,300–$4,399 · Outdoor traditional · Rated up to 4

  • Heater: traditional 6.0kW Harvia electric heater over rocks; solid red cedar staves.
  • Electrical: 240V, 30A hard-wired circuit (professional install required).
  • Max temperature: reaches the traditional 140–190°F range owners report.
  • Warranty: lifetime on the room; 5-year on the heater (heating elements shorter).

Best for: outdoor buyers who want true, high-heat Finnish-style sessions rather than infrared warmth.

Why it stands out: real steam heat, a name-brand Harvia heater, cedar construction, and a lifetime room warranty.

Main limitation: the 240V install is the real cost and complexity; assembly is a multi-hour outdoor project.

Hidden-cost risk: highest in the lineup—electrical plus a level base can add well over a thousand dollars (see the true-cost section).

Owner feedback: owners praise the heat and heater once installed; the recurring frustration is the electrician bill for long 240V runs.

Verdict: the best Costco option for a genuine hot, outdoor sauna—if you’re ready for the wiring, the freight logistics, and manufacturer-only support after the return window. Costco lists the Morgan. If you want traditional-style heat without an outdoor 240V barrel project, the Golden Designs Soria hybrid pairs infrared with a traditional heater indoors—something Costco’s lineup can’t match—with full specialist support behind it.

The seasonal Almost Heaven Arcadia 2P (item 2028780) is a smaller two-person barrel with the same 240V, traditional-heat profile—better for compact yards or couples. The Backyard Discovery Bennett 2–4P (item 4201030663) adds Wi-Fi remote heating and appears seasonally; because it’s a different manufacturer, confirm its exact heater type, electrical spec, and warranty on the live listing before comparing it directly to the Almost Heaven barrels.

Our current Costco sauna picks

Each pick below was validated against current inventory and pricing (August 2026). We don’t hand every model an award—only the categories the evidence supports.

  • Best for most buyers — Dynamic Bellagio 3P. Balance of capacity, price, and 120V simplicity. Tradeoff: curbside delivery and DIY assembly. Buying the same model line through a specialist adds model-matching and lifetime support: shop the Dynamic Bellagio 3-person.
  • Best value / simplest install — Dynamic Gracia 1–2P. Lowest price and the easiest to move and wire. Tradeoff: small capacity. Shop the Dynamic Gracia or the better-value Maxxus Seattle 2-person.
  • Best premium 3-person — Golden Designs Visby 3P. Near-luxury build quality Costco’s lineup doesn’t reach, at roughly a third of a comparable custom sauna’s price. Shop the Golden Designs Visby.
  • Best traditional / high heat / outdoor — Almost Heaven Morgan 4P. Harvia heater, cedar, 140–190°F. Tradeoff: 240V electrical cost and DIY freight. Not carried by InHouse; Costco lists it. For indoor traditional-style heat with support included, consider the Golden Designs Soria hybrid.

What owners and reviewers report: assembly, heat, and EMF

InHouse Wellness hasn’t independently bench-tested these exact units, so rather than invent numbers, the patterns below are drawn from documented owner reviews and published hands-on reviews of the same models. Treat them as directional real-world evidence, not lab data.

Assembly: faster than a barrel, slower than the box claims

For the Dynamic infrared cabins, the “about one hour with two people” figure holds up for a straightforward first build using the clasp-together panel system, and experienced builders report roughly 30–35 minutes on a second assembly. Real-world results vary widely with how much help you have: one Bellagio owner who did nearly the whole thing alone reported it took about six hours across two evenings, while enthusiastic owners with a helper describe it as genuinely quick. A recurring, oddly specific tip from owners: the instruction booklet ships tucked inside the roof section, so open those panels first before hunting through packaging.

Barrel saunas are a different scale of project. Owners of Almost Heaven barrels consistently describe the cabin assembly (staves, bands, roof) as manageable for two people, but the heater and 240V connection as clearly electrician territory. Plan for most of a day.

Assembly and warm-up: claimed vs. owner-reported.
Model Advertised assembly Owner-reported range Heat-up (owner/reviewer)
Dynamic Bellagio 3P (infrared) ~1 hr, 2 people ~30 min (2nd build) to ~6 hrs (mostly solo) ~120°F in 15–20 min; operating temp under 30 min
Almost Heaven barrel (traditional) “Easy for two people” Cabin manageable for 2; heater/240V needs an electrician; ~a day total ~15 min to hot in a cool garage with an 8kW heater

Heat: the infrared-vs-traditional gap is real to owners

Bellagio owners and reviewers describe reaching roughly 120°F in about 15–20 minutes and operating temperature in under half an hour, with 140°F reachable after a longer pre-heat — consistent with the manufacturer’s range and with how radiant infrared feels (the heat works on your body before the air thermometer catches up). Barrel owners tell a different story: one Almost Heaven owner running an 8kW Harvia heater reported the cabin getting hot in about 15 minutes even in a 40–50°F garage, and noted you sweat noticeably faster than in an infrared unit. If your mental image of “sauna” is high, enveloping heat, owner accounts confirm the barrel delivers it and the infrared cabin is a milder, different experience.

Delivery and the curb-to-yard problem show up repeatedly

The most consistent complaint across barrel owners isn’t the sauna — it’s moving it. One Colorado buyer described spending a weekend working out how to get the crate from the driveway to the backyard, then paying roughly $750 for movers with a crane and about $1,200 total beyond the sauna price once electrical and site prep were done. For context, the Almost Heaven Morgan crate weighs about 685 pounds, and larger six-person barrels can top 950–975 pounds. This is the single best argument for planning the last leg (and the electrician) before you order.

EMF: manufacturer numbers, and why independent readings vary

On EMF, the honest picture is more nuanced than any single figure. Dynamic’s own reporting for its low-EMF panels describes roughly 10 mG at about an inch from the panel, ~2 mG at about 10 inches, and ~6 mG at the seated bench position; third-party reviewers of the Bellagio cite a similar 5–10 mG measured 2–3 inches from the panels. Two caveats owners and testers repeatedly surface:

  • Where you measure changes everything. Independent testing of infrared saunas has recorded readings many times higher directly against a rear heating panel than at seated center — one older independent test of a Dynamic unit reported over 60 mG measured about two inches from the rear elements where a user’s back rests. Sitting even a few inches forward of the panels is the practical mitigation.
  • Verification is limited. Reviewers who track EMF methodology note that Dynamic and Maxxus self-report their 5–10 mG figures without naming an independent test lab, whereas some competitors publish seated-position readings from named labs. That doesn’t make the Dynamic numbers wrong, but it means they’re manufacturer figures, and if EMF is a priority you may want the Elite (ultra-low, under ~3 mG) tier or your own meter reading.

The bottom line owners land on: the standard low-EMF Dynamic panels are fine for most users at the seated position, distance matters more than the headline number, and “low EMF” is a comparative claim rather than a verified health benefit.

The true installed cost

The sticker price is the starting line. What changes the math is the work needed to power, place, and assemble the unit. Rather than quote a single national figure, budget by category and apply only the ones your model and home require. The ranges below reflect the Austin-area estimates in our research; your quotes will vary by region, panel age, and distance.

  • Sauna purchase price + sales tax. Start here, and note whether the price you see is a promotion that may expire.
  • 120V dedicated circuit (most Dynamic infrared models): roughly $250–$550 if you need one added; potentially $0 if a compliant dedicated, non-GFCI outlet already exists.
  • 240V circuit, 30–60A (Almost Heaven barrels): roughly $900–$1,800, driven mostly by the run length from panel to yard and whether trenching is involved.
  • Electrical panel upgrade (only if your service is maxed out): roughly $2,000–$4,500.
  • Outdoor base or foundation (barrels): roughly $300–$1,000 for a level gravel pad, concrete, or deck reinforcement.
  • Curb-to-room movement: pallet-jack rental around $50/day, or professional movers roughly $250–$500 for an 800-pound crate.
  • Ongoing: outdoor wood sealant around $60/year; electricity roughly $10–$30/month depending on frequency.
Illustrative total-cost examples (regional estimates; confirm with local quotes).
Model Purchase Likely added costs Illustrative total Confirm before ordering
Bellagio 3P ~$1,999 + ~$300 electrical, ~$50 rental ~$2,350 Do you have a dedicated 20A outlet?
Morgan 4P ~$4,399 + ~$1,200 electrical, ~$500 base ~$6,099 Panel-to-yard 240V run length?

The takeaway: on a 120V infrared cabin, the sticker price is close to the real price. On a 240V barrel, electrical and site prep can add 30–40% or more, which is exactly where a lower sticker becomes less decisive.

Delivery: what Costco includes

Every current Costco sauna listing ships by curbside freight, with a signature required. That means the carrier lowers the crate to ground level at the end of your driveway—and stops there. Curbside delivery does not include moving the crate into a garage, backyard, or room; unpacking; debris removal; or assembly. For barrels like the Morgan, shipping is often serviced directly by the manufacturer.

This is different from parcel delivery, and it’s the single most common surprise owners report. A crate for a 2–4 person sauna can weigh 500–800 pounds, so plan the last leg yourself.

Delivery-day checklist

  • Confirm the appointment window and be present.
  • Have a pallet jack or heavy-duty dollies and 2–4 helpers ready.
  • Lay cardboard or moving blankets along the path to protect floors and thresholds.
  • Inspect the crate for damage before the driver leaves; note damage on the freight bill or refuse delivery.
  • Photograph the crate and any damage immediately.

One genuine Costco advantage on the back end: for returns, freight pickup is included—Costco will arrange collection of the large crate, which specialty retailers don’t always match.

Assembly reality

Manufacturer estimates assume experienced installers under ideal conditions. First-timers should plan for more.

Model type Advertised Real-world (owner reports) Not included in the estimate
Infrared cabin (Bellagio, Gracia) ~45–60 min, 2 people ~1.5–3 hours Unpacking, parts sorting, electrical circuit
Barrel (Morgan, Arcadia) ~4–6 hours ~4–8 hours (often a full day) 240V wiring, base leveling, sealing

Infrared cabins are DIY-friendly with a drill, rubber mallet, level, and one helper. Barrels add band-tightening, roof work, and heater mounting—more skill and two ladders. A useful rule: double the manufacturer’s estimate for your first build, and treat electrical as a separate job, not part of assembly. These figures come from owner videos and reports and are directional rather than precise.

Electrical requirements

Electrical is the difference between a plug-in afternoon and a licensed-electrician project. Requirements by current model:

Model Voltage / amperage Connection Electrician likely?
Gracia 1–2P 120V / 15–20A Dedicated plug (non-GFCI) Only if no dedicated circuit
Bellagio 3P 120V / 20A Dedicated NEMA 5-20P If a new circuit is needed
San Marino Elite 2P 120V (dedicated) Dedicated circuit If a new circuit is needed
Morgan / Arcadia barrel 240V / 30A+ Hard-wired w/ disconnect Yes—licensed electrician required

Two notes worth knowing before you buy: infrared manuals typically specify a dedicated, non-GFCI receptacle, because GFCI outlets can cause nuisance trips with these heaters—so an existing bathroom-style GFCI outlet may not qualify. And older listings sometimes show 15A where the current spec is 20A; follow the higher figure in your model’s manual.

Before you order or install: print your exact model’s installation manual and hand it to a licensed electrician. Confirm voltage, amperage, dedicated-circuit and GFCI requirements, panel capacity, and any permit needs. Improper installation can create a safety hazard and can void the warranty. This guide does not provide wiring instructions.

Temperature and heat experience

Infrared and traditional saunas produce heat differently, and conflating them is the biggest source of disappointment.

  • Dynamic infrared cabins (Bellagio, Gracia, San Marino Elite): manufacturer ranges land around 118–140°F. Infrared warms your body directly by radiant energy, so the air feels cooler than the same “temperature” in a traditional sauna. Owners report reaching the advertised max in roughly 20–30 minutes under typical indoor conditions.
  • Almost Heaven barrels (Morgan, Arcadia): traditional heaters push 140–190°F with hot air and steam—the classic Finnish experience. Warm-up runs longer (often 40–60 minutes) and is affected by outdoor ambient temperature and insulation.

Set expectations by category, not by the word “sauna.” A lower air temperature on an infrared unit doesn’t mean it’s ineffective—the mechanism is different. But if you specifically want high, dry Finnish heat, an infrared cabin will not replicate it.

EMF claims, in context

Infrared marketing leans heavily on “low EMF,” so it’s worth being precise about what that does and doesn’t mean.

  • The figures are manufacturer self-reported. Dynamic/Golden Designs models publish readings around 6–10 mG measured 6–8 inches from the panels (San Marino Elite is marketed as “ultra low”). Independent, standardized testing is limited.
  • Distance dominates. Magnetic field strength drops sharply with distance, so a reading at the panel surface, at six inches, and at the seated position can differ dramatically. A single number without a distance is not meaningful.
  • “Low” is comparative, not zero. Newer carbon panels read lower than older ceramic designs, but any powered device emits some EMF.
  • No consumer standard defines “low EMF” for saunas, and different meters and protocols can’t be compared apples-to-apples.

Importantly, there is no established evidence that lower EMF produces better sauna health outcomes. The clinical literature on sauna safety centers on heat, hydration, and cardiovascular effects—not EMF. If you want to verify a unit yourself, an inexpensive meter can help, but document the exact distances and meter model, and treat generic “6–10 mG” claims as model- and distance-specific rather than universal.

Warranty, returns, and support

Support for a Costco sauna runs through more than one party, and knowing who does what saves frustration.

  • Ordering and delivery damage: Costco. Note damage at delivery and contact Costco for replacement or refund.
  • Early defects and returns (roughly the first 90 days): Costco’s satisfaction guarantee, with freight pickup included for the return.
  • Component failure after the return window: the manufacturer—Golden Designs for Dynamic (phone support line published on their site) or Almost Heaven for the barrels.
  • Warranty terms: Dynamic infrared units carry a 5-year limited warranty on major components; coverage on wood and electronics can be shorter—confirm the specifics for your model. Almost Heaven barrels carry a lifetime warranty on the room and 5 years on the heater, with heating elements typically covered for a shorter period.
  • What’s usually on you: labor to install replacement parts, and damage from improper installation or electrical work.

Two documentation habits pay off: register the product and photograph the serial-number plate on day one, and keep records of every support interaction. There’s a published conflict worth noting—some listings describe the Dynamic warranty as covering wood/electronics for the full 5 years, while the manufacturer’s warranty page describes shorter coverage on those items. Confirm the current terms in writing before you rely on them.

Costco vs. InHouse Wellness

For the Dynamic infrared models, InHouse Wellness stocks the same Bellagio, Gracia, and San Marino Elite model lines. So for those, the decision isn’t about a “better” sauna; it’s about the service around it. (InHouse doesn’t carry Almost Heaven barrels, so for a traditional outdoor barrel your options are Costco or another dealer, while InHouse offers indoor traditional-style heat through hybrids like the Soria.)

Where the channels genuinely differ:

  • Price: Costco is usually lower on the sticker, especially during promotions—a real advantage.
  • Return flexibility: Costco’s satisfaction guarantee and free freight return pickup are more generous than a standard 30-day specialist policy.
  • Pre-sale guidance and expertise: InHouse Wellness is a health-and-wellness sauna specialist—with a certified health coach on staff—who can match a model to your space, electrical situation, and wellness goals before you buy. Costco is self-serve, with no sauna-specific support at the point of sale.
  • Delivery and installation options: InHouse offers optional white-glove delivery and assembly (a service Costco doesn’t provide); Costco’s included delivery is curbside only. White-glove is a paid add-on, not included.
  • Support that doesn’t expire: after Costco’s return window, a Costco buyer is on their own with the manufacturer. InHouse provides lifetime customer support and acts as your liaison on warranty claims—so there’s a real person who knows your unit years later.
  • Bundling: InHouse can package a sauna with accessories, red-light therapy, chromotherapy, cold plunge, and starter kits—often closing much of the sticker-price gap with value Costco doesn’t offer.
  • Selection: InHouse’s Dynamic, Golden Designs, and Maxxus ranges include full-spectrum and hybrid models Costco doesn’t typically stock, such as the Soria hybrid.

Put simply: if the sticker price is what moves your decision and you’re comfortable handling delivery, wiring, and assembly, Costco is a strong choice. If you want the same model line with someone coordinating installation and standing behind the claim process, the specialist route earns its premium.

Who should buy from each channel

Buy from Costco if…

  • A current model genuinely fits your space and heat expectations.
  • Your electrical service is already compatible (a dedicated 120V circuit, or 240V access for a barrel).
  • You can manage curbside delivery and DIY assembly, or hire short-term help.
  • You value the price and the return protection, and accept manufacturer-led support afterward.

Consider a specialist retailer like InHouse Wellness if…

  • You want help choosing between infrared and traditional, or matching a model to your room, panel, and wellness goals—InHouse has a certified health coach on staff for exactly this.
  • Delivery access is difficult, or you want optional white-glove placement and assembly instead of a curbside crate.
  • You want a single point of contact and lifetime support that outlasts a return window, rather than being handed to a manufacturer line after 90 days.
  • You’d rather bundle accessories, red light, or a cold plunge to get more value than a bare sticker price.
  • You need a full-spectrum or hybrid model—like the Maxxus S-Line full-spectrum or Golden Designs Soria hybrid—that Costco doesn’t stock.

Not every buyer needs specialist support—plenty of people do just fine with a plug-in Gracia and an existing outlet. The point is to match the channel to your situation, not to assume one is universally better.

Maintenance in brief

  • Wipe surfaces and let the cabin dry (door open) after every session—this prevents most odor and staining.
  • Clean interior wood with a mild, wood-safe cleaner; clean the glass door as needed.
  • Outdoor barrels: re-seal the exterior wood annually and check the roof.
  • Barrels: re-tighten the metal bands seasonally as the wood swells and shrinks.
  • Inspect heater stones (barrels) and control connections periodically.
  • Always follow your model’s manual for approved products and intervals.

Health and safety, briefly

Regular sauna use is generally safe for healthy adults, and observational research—most notably Finnish cohort studies using traditional high-heat saunas—associates frequent use with lower cardiovascular mortality, though only at four to seven sessions a week. The intervals, and where the evidence stops. (Laukkanen et al., 2018). Two caveats matter for buyers: those are associations, not proof of cause, and the strongest data come from traditional saunas, not lower-temperature infrared cabins, where long-term evidence is more limited. General sauna research does not establish that any specific Costco product delivers superior health outcomes.

The most relevant acute risks are dehydration, lightheadedness, and transient blood-pressure changes; avoid alcohol during sessions and keep durations moderate (commonly 15–20 minutes). See our overview of sauna health benefits and how often to use a sauna for more.

This article is for general information and is not medical advice. People with cardiovascular conditions, pregnancy, heat intolerance, or medications affecting blood pressure or hydration should seek individualized medical guidance before sauna use.

Common myths, corrected

  1. “Free shipping means it comes to my door.” Costco sauna delivery is curbside freight—the crate stops at your driveway, and moving an 800-pound box is your job.
  2. “Infrared saunas get as hot as traditional ones.” Dynamic infrared units max around 140°F; traditional barrels run 140–190°F. The infrared experience is radiant, not high-ambient-air heat.
  3. “Low EMF means zero EMF.” Published figures are roughly 6–10 mG near the panels at a stated distance. “Low” is comparative; distance is your best mitigation.
  4. “Any sauna plugs into a normal outlet.” Infrared cabins need a dedicated (often non-GFCI) circuit; barrel saunas require 240V hard-wiring.
  5. “Assembly takes 45 minutes.” That’s an ideal-conditions estimate. First-timers should expect 1.5–3 hours for infrared and 4–8 hours for a barrel, excluding electrical.
  6. “Costco’s return policy and the manufacturer warranty are the same thing.” They’re separate. Costco handles early returns; the manufacturer handles component warranty afterward.

FAQ

How much do Costco saunas currently cost?

As checked in August 2026, infrared cabins ranged from roughly $1,799 (Gracia) to about $2,499 (San Marino Elite), with the Bellagio around $1,999 on a $500 promotion. Barrel saunas ran roughly $3,000–$4,400. Confirm live pricing, since promotions rotate.

What sauna brands does Costco sell?

Primarily Dynamic (indoor infrared, made by Golden Designs) and Almost Heaven (outdoor traditional barrels, owned by Harvia), with occasional models from other makers such as Backyard Discovery.

What is the best current Costco sauna?

For most indoor buyers, the Dynamic Bellagio 3-person balances capacity, price, and 120V simplicity. For a true high-heat outdoor sauna, the Almost Heaven Morgan barrel.

Does Costco deliver saunas inside?

No. Current listings are curbside freight only. Plan for equipment and helpers to move the crate from the curb to its final spot.

Do Costco saunas require an electrician?

Barrel saunas always need a licensed electrician for 240V hard-wiring. Infrared cabins need a dedicated 120V circuit—which may already exist, but often needs an electrician to add or confirm.

How hot do Costco infrared saunas get?

Roughly 118–140°F. Infrared warms the body directly, so the air feels cooler than a traditional sauna at the same number.

Are Costco saunas really low EMF?

Manufacturers label many models “low EMF,” citing about 6–10 mG at 6–8 inches. That’s comparative, not zero, and independent verification is limited. There’s no evidence that lower EMF improves health outcomes.

Can a Costco infrared sauna go outdoors?

Most Dynamic infrared cabins are built for indoor, climate-controlled spaces; outdoor use can void the warranty and accelerate wear. For outdoors, choose a purpose-built barrel or a model rated for weather exposure.

What happens if the sauna breaks after the return window?

You work with the manufacturer under their limited warranty—Golden Designs for Dynamic, Almost Heaven for the barrels. Keep your serial number and proof of purchase; note that labor to install parts is usually your responsibility.

Is Costco or a specialist retailer better for a sauna?

Costco tends to win on the sticker price and return flexibility. A specialist like InHouse Wellness wins on pre-sale guidance from a certified health coach, optional white-glove installation, lifetime support and warranty-claim help, product bundling, and a wider selection (full-spectrum and hybrid models Costco doesn’t stock). Because the Dynamic model lines match, the choice comes down to whether you want the lowest upfront number or the same model line with the service and support around it.

Final verdict

Costco saunas can be genuine values—particularly the Dynamic Bellagio for indoor infrared and the Almost Heaven Morgan for outdoor high heat. The catch is that the advertised price only tells part of the story. The purchase is strongest when you’ve already confirmed electrical compatibility, delivery access, and assembly, and when you’re comfortable with manufacturer-led support after the return window.

The sticker becomes less decisive the moment you factor in a new 240V circuit, difficult crate placement, professional assembly, and support that ends when the return window does. That’s the real gap: because the Dynamic model lines match, buying through InHouse Wellness gets you the same model line plus model-matching from a certified health coach, lifetime customer support, a warranty liaison, optional white-glove installation, and the ability to bundle accessories or a red-light upgrade—value that often narrows or erases the price difference once you total everything up. In the end, the exact SKU and your home’s readiness matter far more than the word “Costco.”
